title: Django
notes: The project that django-admin startproject generates, with all its default apps and middleware, served over WSGI by Waitress on 4 threads in one process. No request opens the database.
details: A project newly generated by `django-admin startproject` (Django's default settings, synchronous views), deployed as its documentation says: on a WSGI server. Served through the generated config/wsgi.py by Waitress with its defaults (4 worker threads, HTTP/1.1 keep-alive), started on a thread inside the one measured process; Django's documentation names Gunicorn, uWSGI and mod_wsgi, which all hand requests to worker processes, so the pure-Python threaded Waitress stands in for them under the one-process rule. Waitress's queue-depth warnings are silenced, as request logging is. Differs from the generated project only in DEBUG = False and ALLOWED_HOSTS = ['127.0.0.1'] (the SECRET_KEY is the one startproject generated, kept fixed); all six default apps with the admin and its URLs, all seven middleware, the three context processors and the sqlite DATABASES entry are as generated, and no request opens the database (sessions and users are lazy; db.sqlite3 is never created). The shop is one app, `shop`, made with `startapp` and added to INSTALLED_APPS and to the URLconf; /about is a TemplateView, rendered from a template with no data on each request since Django has no build-time prerendering.
